transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I guess what brought me in is... I had an incident the other day. I volunteer, and I just completely blew up at one of the younger volunteers. 

It was over something silly, really—just a crooked tablecloth. But I really lost my temper and let them have it. I don't usually talk to people that way... it's just not like me at all. So, I figured I had better come in and talk to somebody about it.
Over the past few weeks or months, before this incident with the tablecloth, have you been feeling more irritable or having a shorter temper than usual?

No, not really. That's why it caught me so off guard. Before that day, things were pretty normal. I haven't been snapping at anyone or feeling particularly on edge, just going about my usual routine. That's why the whole thing with the tablecloth was so strange for me.
Have you had any other episodes like this—where you suddenly lost your temper or acted in a way that felt out of character—either before the tablecloth incident or since then?

No, nothing else like that. It really was just that one time at the volunteer center. Since then, and even before, I haven't had any other outbursts or anything that felt like that. It was just a one-off thing, as far as I can tell.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or depressed for most of the day on most days?

No, I haven't been feeling down or depressed. I mean, I'm getting older, so I have my days where my joints ache and I might not feel like doing much, but... no, not sad or anything like that. Just my usual self, really.
Did anything stressful or upsetting happen in the days or weeks right before you had that incident with the tablecloth at the volunteer center?

Well, yes, there was. This whole thing has been going on for about a week now... ever since there was a robbery right outside the bank. That happened just a little bit before the incident at the volunteer center.
Since the bank robbery happened, have you been having unwanted memories or flashbacks about it, or disturbing dreams about it at night?

Yes, actually. It's... it's strange. Out of nowhere, I'll just hear that man's rough voice in my head. Or I'll see the donation envelope hitting the ground again. It happens even when I'm just sitting quietly at my kitchen table, having my coffee. It just pops into my mind when I don't want it to.
Since the bank robbery, have you noticed that you're more jumpy or easily startled by sudden noises or movements?

Yes, I have. Just the other day, a car backfired over near the senior center, and... well, I jumped so hard my chest actually hurt. My hands just kept shaking for a few minutes after that, too. So, yes, I definitely am.
Since the bank robbery, have you been trying to avoid certain places, people, or situations that remind you of what happened?

Yes, I have. I've been... well, taking the long way around on my walks just so I don't have to pass by the bank. And I haven't gone into the festival storage room, either. Going in there just brings the whole thing a bit too close, so I've just been staying away.
When did these flashbacks, jumpiness, and avoidance behaviors first start after the bank robbery—did they begin right away that same day, or did they start a few days later?
Well, it all started pretty much right after it happened. It's been going on for about a week now, ever since that day outside the bank.
Are these symptoms—the flashbacks, the jumpiness, the avoidance—still happening now, or have they started to get better over this past week?

Well, they're still happening. I'm not really sure if they've started to get better or not, to be honest with you. It's only been a week, so... I guess I just haven't noticed much of a change yet. They're definitely still there, though.
You mentioned the bank robbery happened about a week ago. Just to be clear, are these symptoms—the flashbacks, the jumpiness, and avoiding places—things that are still bothering you today, right now?
Yes, they are. They're still happening today. I mean, I'm still feeling jumpy and... well, I'm still avoiding the bank and the storage room. It's all still going on right now.

You mentioned the bank robbery happened about a week ago. Just to make sure I have the timeline right—these flashbacks, the jumpiness, and the avoidance have been going on continuously for all seven days since it happened, correct? Or did they start a few days after the robbery?
Yes, that's correct. They didn't start a few days later. This has been going on continuously for about a week now, ever since the robbery outside the bank.

F43.10 (Acute stress disorder, unspecified) is the appropriate diagnosis given the acute timeline and symptom cluster.
